about: GPS: how your phone knows where you are. Clocks in space, the four-satellite fix, and why Einstein's relativity has to be corrected (NTS-2, 1977). Factory #4. Narration-led: the voice is recorded first and every visual beat is keyed to its word times.

lines.text: Your phone finds you using clocks in space.
So how does GPS work? And why does it need Einstein?
lines.say: So how does G.P.S. work? And why does it need Einstein?

lines.text: About 30 GPS satellites circle Earth, over 12,000 miles up.
lines.say: About thirty G.P.S. satellites circle Earth, over twelve thousand miles up.

lines.text: Each one broadcasts two things: the time, and where it is.
Here's the trick: your phone never talks back. It only listens.
The signal reaches you in under a tenth of a second.
lines.say: The signal reaches you, in under a tenth of a second.

lines.text: Trip time, times the speed of light, equals distance.
Three satellites, three distances: you're pinned to one spot.
But light goes about a foot every billionth of a second.
Your phone's clock isn't that good. A fourth satellite fixes it.
Now the weird part: weaker gravity up there makes clocks tick faster.
Their speed, about 8,700 miles an hour, slows them a little.
lines.say: Their speed, about eighty-seven hundred miles an hour, slows them a little.

lines.text: Net result: they run 38 millionths of a second fast, every day.
lines.say: Net result: they run thirty-eight millionths of a second fast, every day.

lines.text: At light speed, that's about seven miles of distance error a day.
Back in 1977, not everyone believed that would matter.
lines.say: Back in nineteen seventy-seven, not everyone believed that would matter.

lines.text: So a test satellite flew its atomic clock with the fix off.
For twenty days it ran fast, almost exactly as Einstein predicted.
Since then, every GPS clock gets corrected for it.
lines.say: Since then, every G.P.S. clock gets corrected for it.

lines.text: That's how your phone finds you within about 16 feet.
lines.say: That's how your phone finds you within about sixteen feet.

lines.text: It's Einstein, built into the blue dot on your map.
